strings.libraryHint: Drag a block onto the canvas or click to add it.
strings.headline: Build your own vision.
strings.previewHint: Gain and grey zero affect only the display. Calculations preserve the original numerical values.
strings.exampleHint: Learning examples show a single operation. Python export saves the complete current algorithm.
strings.firstDifference: The first frame after an algorithm change has zero difference.
strings.confidenceHint: A is a derived saturation estimate, not measured transparency or probability.
strings.enabled: Operation enabled (off passes the input through)
strings.missingLesson: The learning package is missing. Open the repository documentation.
strings.draft: Machine translation · check the English original.
strings.exists: The difference block is already on the canvas. Select it for its explanation.
strings.stateSaved: State saved locally and downloaded as JSON.
strings.exported: Python algorithm exported. Requires NumPy and OpenCV.
strings.confirmOpen: Open the project and discard unsaved changes?
strings.confirmImport: Import the project and discard unsaved changes?
strings.noProjects: No saved projects. Import JSON or save the current state.
strings.mediaLarge: The maximum source size is 100 MB.
strings.resized: Preview resized to a maximum of 960 px
strings.ended: The source has stopped delivering frames.
strings.codeHint: Custom code runs on Apply or Run. It has your user permissions on this computer; run only code you trust. An empty block passes its input through.
strings.codeContract: Python: process(channels, params) → H × W array. JavaScript: process(channels, params, shape) → flat H × W values. All upstream channels are available; params.gain is adjustable.
strings.needsCodeRun: Code is ready. Choose Apply, Run or Single frame to execute.
strings.incompatible: No compatible implementation for this block
strings.runtimeHint: This choice controls execution. The lesson example language is a separate setting.
strings.adaptationHint: Modern adaptation of part of the original example. Template matching, robotics and calibrated measurements are not included.
strings.legacyHint: Original SimpleCV/Python 2 example: reference requiring adaptation for the current runtime.
strings.apiHint: Installed OpenCV reference. To execute, use a custom Python block returning one H × W channel.
strings.recipeHint: Opens a saved recipe with all required upstream blocks.
strings.moreCatalog: All matches are available in the dropdown.
strings.engineScope: The selected version executes supported processing blocks. Capture, display and image transfer remain shared by the application.
strings.api24Hint: OpenCV 2.4.13.7 source reference. Library blocks run native operations; custom Python uses the limited cv24.run bridge.
strings.languageId: Language ID (for example: rust, java, cpp)
strings.adapterReady: An execution adapter is available for this language and engine.
strings.draftOnly: No compatible execution adapter is installed. You can write and save code; this block passes its input through until an adapter is configured.
strings.codeDraftSaved: Code kept in the block without execution. Save the project to keep it on disk.
strings.cCodeContract: C11: void process(const SmContext *ctx, float *out). Read channels with sm_channel(ctx, "R"); write all ctx->rows * ctx->cols values. Parameters: ctx->input, ctx->gain, ctx->backend.
strings.cppCodeContract: C++17: void process(const SmContext& ctx, float *out). Read channels with sm_channel(&ctx, "R"); write all ctx.rows * ctx.cols values. Parameters: ctx.input, ctx.gain, ctx.backend.
strings.javaCodeContract: Java: public static float[] process(Map<String, float[]> channels, Params p). Return p.rows * p.cols values. Parameters: p.input, p.gain, p.backend. Write methods here; the application supplies the UserBlock class.
strings.compiledHint: The first run compiles your code (up to 30 seconds). Later frames reuse the build. The block time limit applies to execution. These adapters process float channels; OpenCV operations remain separate blocks in the selected engine.
strings.blockMathRuntime: This block runs as compiled code in the selected language.
strings.blockVisionRuntime: The selected language uses an adapter to the shared OpenCV engine. The algorithm and OpenCV version stay the same.
